newsitem.title: FRANCE: French government allows Snecma to buy out SEP.
newsitem.headline: French government allows Snecma to buy out SEP.

text.p: The French government has approved a plan by aero-engine maker Snecma to make a public offer to buy out minorities of rocket engine manufacturer SEP, to take its stake to 100 from 51 percent, the finance ministry said on Wednesday.

"The government has been advised of Snecma's wish to raise its holding in the capital of SEP from 51 percent to 100 percent and has given its approval so Snecma's board can make a public offer for SEP shares, followed by, if the 95 percent threshold is reached, a mandatory buy-in," the ministry said.
The transaction offers a strong industrial logic and would ensure Snecma's future in space programmes and assures its position as France's centre for engine capabilities, it said.
The move would also consolidate Snecma's brakes activities by bringing together the industrial and technological skills of SEP, Carbone Industrie and Messier Bugatti.
It will create a strategic missile centre in the the Aquitaine region, with a view to building a champion in large propulsion systems.

The government sees the project as a consolidation of French industrial and technological potential, which will allow the new group to play a "federating" role in European and international alliances.
The government approved the Snecma plan to offer SEP minority shareholders an exit, which would meet conditions of the stock market and ensure a free choice, the ministry statement said.
The Societe Europeene de Propulsion (SEP) makes engines and boosters for the Ariane rockets, used by the European Arianespace consortium.
